To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have isolated and characterized a number of recombinant plasmids containing sequences homologous with RNAs expressed at a high abundance in the myeloblasts of acute non-lymphocytic leukaemia (ANLL) patients.

the RNA dot hybridization method has been used to measure the relative abundances of myeloid lineage RNAs in total RNA samples isolated from peripheral blood leucocytes from leukaemia patients and normal individuals, with the results showing that these probes have potential to subdivide the ANLLs, and extend a molecular classification to the myeloid lineage leukaemias.
we have constructed recombinant plasmid cDNa libraries representing the polyA ^{+} RNAs in the human myeloid cell line KG1 and the murine myeloid cell ML1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes that are expressed in the myeloblasts of ANLL and CML.

the identification of molecular probes which can be used to characterise the expression of genes in the leukaemic cells and which may be used to identify the molecular basis for the heterogeneity of the myelodysplastic and leukaemic disorders.
the development and application of molecular hybridisation probes for the detection and quantitation of specific RNAs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data presented are consistent with the following conclusions: i) the probes are homologous to RNA sequences expressed in the myeloblasts and monoblasts; ii) the RNA sequences are not expressed in normal bone marrow or peripheral blood; iii) the probes are not homologous to any of the RNAs expressed in normal T lymphocytes; and iv) the probes are expressed in the majority of ANLL and acute-phase CML patients.
the probes have the potential for the molecular classification of the acute leukaemias.
these probes are not specific for ANLL but are useful in distinguishing the ANLLs from other leukaemias and normal individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have isolated and characterised three molecular hybridisation probes, pML15 (1.4 kb), pKG21 (1.5 kb) and pKGA-F5 (1.5kb).
we have identified three new molecular hybridisation probes which are useful in the molecular characterisation of the myeloblasts in acute myelogenous leukaemias.
we have identified three recombinants which contain sequences homolgous to RNAs which are expressed at high abundance by myeloid cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a number of clones which contain cDNA sequences homologous in the myeloblasts.
the use of recombinant plasmid cDNDs as probes for RNA dot hybridisation is an extremely powerful method for the detection of specific RNAs in total RNA samples.
we can identify a number of clones which are highly expressed in myeloid cell types and are expressed at lower levels or not at all in normal cells.
